beats.text: For most of history, making fire took real skill.
Early humans spun a stick against wood, until the friction made a glowing ember.
Later, striking flint on iron threw sparks onto dry tinder. Ötzi the Iceman carried a fire kit over five thousand years ago.
In 1826, John Walker invented the friction match, by accident.
Safety matches only lit when struck on their own box.
Pocket lighters made a flame with a flick of a wheel.
Today, a stove lights with a click, and induction cooktops cook with no flame at all.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
